project.name: osgi/jgiven
project.description: BDD-in-OSGi test tooling. jGiven runs its scenarios in-container THROUGH the host bundle's classloader, so it is a BDD concern, not a JUnit-scoped one — it depends on the junit testkit (osgi/testkit) but is not owned by it. Holds the durable result of the jgiven-osgi-bundle spike: jgiven-wrap (jgiven wrapped as a first-class bundle, test-scope), jgiven-testkit (the reusable shared bnd include for the one forced fragment import + the JGivenTestkit boot helper), and a probe host bundle with its sibling -test fragment + harness that double as the palier-2/3 non-regression guard — the guard models the real convention (a -test fragment alongside its host bundle) and runs IN-CONTAINER thanks to jgiven-testkit + jgiven-wrap, so it IS the template a host like doctor copies. See docs/architecture/osgi/jgiven-osgi-testkit-handoff.adoc.
